# What’s new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026
At [Ignite 2026](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/home) , Foundry Agent Service delivers new capabilities to get you there across the agent lifecycle: Build, Deploy, and Operate.
Build more capable agents faster with the managed Microsoft Copilot harness, real-time voice, and richer tool connections. Deploy them at scale with enterprise controls, and bring them into Microsoft 365 where people already work. Operate them with confidence by turning production evidence into validated improvements. Here’s what’s new, and how each capability helps you move from idea to impact.

## Build: Create agents on your terms
### Build harness agents with the tools you use
[The Microsoft Copilot harness](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/use-tools-skills-copilot-harness?tabs=python&pivots=portal) , in public preview, gives developers a fully managed way to build prompt agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox; you bring the knowledge, reusable skills, and connected tools that make the agent yours.

...

### Voice conversations to your agents, now generally available
Talking to AI should feel as natural as talking to a person. [Voice agents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/configure-voice-agent?pivots=foundry-portal) in Foundry Agent Service are now generally available, giving organizations an enterprise-grade way to add real-time voice to their agents. That covers serving customers, supporting employees, and powering in-car and in-app assistants.
* **Conversations that feel human:** people can interrupt, pause and change direction, and the agent keeps up.
* **Builds on what you already have:** add voice to existing agents without rewriting them, and connect to phone and contact center systems through native telephony.
* **Production-ready from day one:** build, deploy, monitor and improve voice agents on the same managed platform as the rest of your agents.
Thousands of customers have adopted voice agents since public preview, across customer service, automotive, education, HR and public services. [**[Read what’s new in Azure Speech in Foundry Tools→]**](https://aka.ms/azure-speech-ignite-26-blog)

### Connect tools and act across applications
At Ignite, we’re expanding how Foundry agents connect to tools, business context, and other agents. Work IQ and Fabric IQ integrations, in preview, bring Microsoft 365 context and Fabric data into agent workflows. Web Search powered by Web IQ is generally available for prompt agents, with Toolbox support coming soon, while the generally available A2A tool connects Foundry and external agents.
Toolboxes make these capabilities reusable through a managed MCP endpoint, with expanded skills support, a monitoring dashboard, and preview tool policies.
Computer use and browser automation are now generally available for tasks that require an application interface rather than an API. Browser automation combines isolated browser sessions with Live View and Take control for human oversight, session recordings in customer-owned storage, and preview access to applications behind private virtual networks.

...

## Deploy: Put agents to work at scale
### Run hosted agents with less friction
* **Shared subnet IPs — GA:** Sessions share subnet IP addresses while retaining their own VM-isolated sandboxes, reducing pressure on private IP capacity. Default quotas are 1,000–2,000 concurrent sessions per subscription and region, with increases available on request.
* **Memory snapshots — Public preview:** Reduce cold starts by restoring an initialized agent state instead of repeatedly loading libraries and data.

...

* **Private certificate authority trust — Public preview:** Connect to internal APIs, MCP servers, and model gateways that use your organization’s certificates. Register your CA at the Foundry resource level while keeping certificate and hostname validation enabled.
* **Azure Policy governance — Public preview:** Require approved egress configurations across subscriptions or resource groups.

...

When a session goes idle, compute is released and its state is saved, so the agent picks up where it left off on the next request.
* **Deployment to customer-owned AKS — Coming soon; public preview targeted for early December:** Use the Foundry APIs and developer workflow while running agents on your own AKS clusters. Foundry manages the service integration; your team operates the cluster, networking, and capacity.

...

### Bring agents into everyday work with Microsoft 365 accounts
Foundry is integrating with **[Microsoft 365 Resources for Agents](http://aka.ms/microsoft-365-resources-for-agents)** , which equips supported agents with their own secured Microsoft 365 resources, including a standalone mailbox, calendar, and OneDrive workspace for file storage. These capabilities will be made available to supported agents across the Microsoft portfolio.

...

## Operate: Govern and continuously improve
* **Insights — GA:** Identify recurring issues across production traces, see supporting evidence, and investigate likely causes. This visibility also extends to agents built with LangGraph, LangChain, and CrewAI.
* **Annotations on traces — Public preview:** Capture expert feedback on what worked, what didn’t, and what the agent should have done. Evaluation datasets, in preview, turn those reviews into reusable tests for future versions.
* **Insights to Agent Optimizer — Preview:** Send a recurring production issue to Agent Optimizer to generate candidate fixes and test them against your evaluations.
* **Skill optimization — Preview:** Turn past interactions and expert feedback into new or improved skills. Versioned skills can be reused or rolled back; the running agent changes only when your team adopts an update.
* **Cost optimization — Public preview:** Find more cost-efficient model choices without compromising quality, with candidate changes evaluated before your team decides what to ship.
Every improvement should be validated before release and monitored afterward. For the full continuous improvement story, see [Tina Schuchman’s blog](https://aka.ms/ignite26Foundry) .

...

## Start building
* [Explore Foundry Agent Service Learn Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)
If you’re attending Microsoft Ignite 2026, or watching on-demand content later, be sure to check out these sessions:
1. [BRK240: Build and scale the next generation of AI agents in Microsoft Foundry](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/sessions/1787856609563001Ep0b-1791588070636001Coui?source=sessions)

3. [BRK243: How much should you own?

# What's new in Azure API Management at Microsoft Ignite 2026
## Accelerate AI development. Govern AI interactions. Scale with confidence.
At Microsoft Ignite 2026, we're announcing the general availability of Azure AI Gateway and new capabilities in Azure API Management to help organizations accelerate development, extend enterprise governance to AI interactions, and scale with confidence.

...

### Azure AI Gateway is now generally available
* **Accelerate AI development:** Connect to models and MCP tools across providers using stable aliases, flexible routing, and automatic failover. Model Router (preview) can also select models based on cost or quality objectives.
* **Govern and observe AI interactions:** Centralize identity, access policies, content safety, and observability across model and tool calls.

...

### Extend governance to AI agents and tools
The **Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway** is now generally available , connecting centralized agent governance with runtime enforcement. Organizations can discover supported gateways and MCP servers, manage access policies, enforce supported tool restrictions, and monitor interactions for security and auditing.

...

### Scale enterprise APIs across more regions
Azure API Management **Premium v2 is now available in 35 Azure regions** , giving organizations greater flexibility to deploy enterprise APIs closer to applications and users while meeting regional deployment requirements. Customers can provision Premium v2 instances through the Azure portal, REST APIs, Bicep, or Azure Resource Manager templates.
[See the full list of supported regions.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-region-availability)

### Building the future of enterprise API and AI governance
With the innovations announced at Microsoft Ignite 2026, we're helping organizations build AI applications faster, extend governance across APIs and AI interactions, and scale enterprise workloads with the security, visibility, and control their businesses require.

...

### Join us at Microsoft Ignite 2026
Stop by the **Serverless Apps and Agents booth** to meet our product team, see the latest capabilities, and share what you're building.
We look forward to seeing you there!

# What's new in Azure Functions and Durable Task Scheduler at Microsoft Ignite 2026
## A technical walkthrough of the GA and public preview updates across Managed Connectors, Flex Consumption, Durable Task Scheduler, agentic workflows, language runtimes, and developer tooling.
At Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re announcing a significant set of updates across Azure Functions and Durable Task Framework.
The releases cover everything from new integration capabilities and custom containers on Flex Consumption to durable execution for AI applications, enterprise security and resilience, new language runtimes, and improvements to the tools developers use to build, deploy, and troubleshoot their

...

### At a glance: Microsoft Ignite 2026 announcements
| Area | What's new | Status | Learn more |
| **Managed Connectors** | Managed Connectors in Azure Functions ( `ConnectorTrigger` with webhook + outbound polling modes, and outbound SDK) | **GA** | [Blog](https://aka.ms/managed-connectors-functions-blog-ga) · [Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-connectors-overview) · [Samples](https://aka.ms/functions-connectors-samples) |
| **Flex Consumption containers and deployment** | Custom Linux containers for OS-level dependencies, plus deployment validation logging in audit mode | **Public Preview** * | [Blog](https://aka.ms/flex-container-blog) · [Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/flex-consumption-os-level-dependencies) · [Samples](https://aka.ms/flex-container-sample-dotnet) |
| **Durable Task SDKs & Durable Task Scheduler** | **GA:** Durable Extension for Microsoft Agent Framework, Customer-managed keys (CMK), Private endpoints **Preview*:** Durable execution for LangGraph & Pydantic AI, Native disaster recovery, Task Queues, Durable Task SDK for Go | **GA & Public Preview** * | [DTS Ignite blog](https://aka.ms/dts-ignite-2026) · [Agent Framework blog](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/durable-task-extension-for-microsoft-agent-framework-is-now-generally-available/4571100) · [Go SDK](https://github.com/microsoft/durabletask-go) |
| **Agentic functions & AI authoring** | Azure Functions Hosted Skill and agent bindings (Python), Dynamic Workflows updates, and Azure Functions Canvas and Skills | **Public Preview** * | [Hosted Skills](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-hosted-skills) · [Agent bindings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-agent-bindings) · [Dynamic Workflows](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/enable-dynamic-workflows-in-azure-functions-hosted-skills/4551993) · [Canvas](https://awesome-copilot.github.com/extension/azure-functions/) · [Skills docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-skills) |
| **Language runtimes & workers** | **GA:** Golang on Flex Consumption, .NET 11 **Preview*:** Python 3.15 (Rust worker transport), Node.js 26 | **GA & Public Preview** * | [Go docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-reference-go) · [.NET 11 blog](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/-net-11-is-now-generally-available-in-azure-functions/4571176) · [Python 3.15 blog](https://aka.ms/azurefunctions/python/315-architecture) · [Runtimes matrix](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/supported-languages) |
| **Developer CLI & diagnostics** | Azure Functions CLI (v5) and Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2 | **Public Preview** * | [CLI docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-cli-develop-local) · [CLI repo](https://github.com/azure/azure-functions-cli) · [Network Troubleshooter blog](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/azure-functions-network-troubleshooter-and-connectivity-checks-/4573917) |

## Trigger functions from SaaS events and call enterprise APIs with Managed Connectors
### Managed Connectors in Azure Functions (GA)
Managed Connectors in Azure Functions is now generally available together with [Azure Connector Namespace](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/integrationsonazureblog/connector-namespace-is-generally-available/4573019) (also GA), supporting .NET isolated, Python, and Node.js.

...

## Stateful orchestrations and enterprise controls in Durable Task Scheduler
Durable Task Scheduler (DTS) is the managed backend for Durable Functions, Durable Task SDK workers, and stateful agents. At Ignite 2026, updates expand DTS across enterprise security, regional resilience, rate control, Go orchestration authoring, and durable agent execution.
_Figure 3: Enterprise topology for Durable Task Scheduler combining VNet private endpoints, customer-managed keys in Key Vault or Managed HSM, task queues, and active-passive regional disaster recovery._

...

* **Durable agents — Durable Extension for Microsoft Agent Framework (GA), LangGraph (Public Preview*), and Pydantic AI:** The [Durable Extension for Microsoft Agent Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/hosting/durable-extension) is generally available for .NET ( `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.AzureFunctions` ) and Python ( `agent-framework-azurefunctions` ), persisting agent conversation state,

...

* **Native disaster recovery (Public Preview*):** Replicates task hub state across paired primary and secondary regions for unplanned failover and zero-drain planned failover ( [docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/durable-task/scheduler/disaster-recovery) ).

...

* **Durable Task SDK for Go (Public Preview*):** Brings code-first orchestrations, activities, fan-out/fan-in, external events, durable timers, and retry policies to Go 1.25+ ( [`microsoft/durabletask-go`](https://github.com/microsoft/durabletask-go) ), powering `middleware/durabletask` in the Azure Functions Go worker.

...

## Agentic functions, bindings, and AI-assisted development
### Azure Functions Canvas and Azure Functions Skills (Public Preview*)
**Azure Functions Canvas** is built for developers using the GitHub Copilot app and VS Code, with an early release available now as part of Awesome Copilot ( [Azure Functions | Awesome GitHub Copilot](https://awesome-copilot.github.com/extension/azure-functions/) ). It provides an interactive workspace to build and manage Azure Functions apps with AI coding tools:
* **Template system built for AI coding:** Go from create to build, local test, and deploy while using fewer tokens and waiting less. Previously, using an official template alongside an AI coding tool required opening Visual Studio or VS Code; you can now complete the entire workflow without leaving the GitHub Copilot app.
* **Modernize:** Identifies runtime versions, language versions, and hosting SKUs that are out of support or approaching end of support, then helps migrate your project to the latest versions and programming models.
* **Localized UI:** The Canvas panel is available in 7 languages.

...

## Language runtime updates: Go, .NET 11, Python 3.15, and Node.js 26
| Language | Version | Status | Supported hosting plans | Notable architecture change |
| **Go** | Go 1.24+ | **GA** | Flex Consumption | Native gRPC worker ( `azure-functions-golang-worker` ) replaces HTTP custom handlers |
| **.NET** | .NET 11 STS (.NET isolated model) | **GA** | All active Azure Functions hosting plans | `Azure.Functions.Sdk` MSBuild SDK and rootless chiseled base images |
| **Python** | Python 3.15 | **Public Preview** * | Flex Consumption, Elastic Premium, Dedicated (Linux) | Rust-based worker transport embeds CPython, removing worker `grpcio` / `protobuf` conflicts |
| **Node.js** | Node.js 26 | **Public Preview** * | Flex Consumption, Elastic Premium, Dedicated (Linux) | Early runtime and npm compatibility validation on the v4 programming model |

...

## Azure Functions CLI (v5) and Network Troubleshooter v2
### Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2 (Public Preview*)
On Dedicated, Elastic Premium, and Windows Consumption, it runs live connectivity, DNS, TCP, firewall, and RBAC checks; on **Flex Consumption** , it performs static ARM and control-plane validation across app VNet/DNS settings, destination firewalls/private endpoints/NSGs/Private DNS zone links, and Managed Identity RBAC roles.

...

## Companion blog posts and engineering deep dives
If you made it this far and want more, we got you! Our PMs and engineers published companion announcement and architecture deep-dive posts across these releases:

...

* **Durable Task Scheduler, SDKs, and agentic workflows**
+ [What's new in Azure Functions Durable Task Scheduler at Microsoft Ignite 2026](https://aka.ms/dts-ignite-2026)
+ [Durable Task Extension for Microsoft Agent Framework is now Generally Available](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/durable-task-extension-for-microsoft-agent-framework-is-now-generally-available/4571100)

...
